source.title: Watershed Boundary Dataset (WBD), 2-digit Hydrologic Unit regions

legend.gulf-of-california: Colorado River system → Gulf of California
legend.gulf-of-mexico: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico (Atlantic)

divide.name: Continental Divide (drawn as the boundary between Pacific- and Gulf-bound USGS regions)

regions.name: Texas Gulf
regions.destinationLabel: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico (Atlantic)
regions.drainsTo: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico through Texas rivers such as the Brazos and the Colorado of Texas.

regions.name: Rio Grande
regions.destinationLabel: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico (Atlantic)
regions.drainsTo: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico through the Rio Grande, the river shared by the U.S. and Mexico.

regions.name: Upper Colorado
regions.destinationLabel: Colorado River system → Gulf of California
regions.drainsTo: Snowmelt from the Rockies of Colorado, Wyoming, Utah and New Mexico gathers in the Green, Gunnison and San Juan rivers and the upper Colorado, above Lee Ferry.

regions.name: Arkansas–White–Red
regions.destinationLabel: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico (Atlantic)
regions.drainsTo: Drains east through the Arkansas and Red rivers to the Mississippi.

regions.name: Great Basin
regions.drainsTo: Drains nowhere: rivers end in lakes and playas (Great Salt Lake, Pyramid Lake, Humboldt and Carson sinks) and the water leaves by evaporation.

regions.name: California
regions.drainsTo: Most of California drains to the Pacific through the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta and San Francisco Bay; the Tulare basin is closed in most years.

regions.name: Lower Colorado
regions.destinationLabel: Colorado River system → Gulf of California
regions.drainsTo: Below Lee Ferry the Colorado runs through the Grand Canyon to Lake Mead and on to Mexico; today nearly all of it is diverted before the Gulf of California.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest
regions.drainsTo: Drains to the Pacific through the Columbia River; the Snake River is its largest tributary.

regions.name: Missouri
regions.destinationLabel: Drains to the Gulf of Mexico (Atlantic)
regions.drainsTo: Drains east through the Missouri River to the Mississippi and the Gulf of Mexico; includes the North Platte.
